content.text:
Review complete. Here's the full picture.

## State of the branch

`feat/gemini-live-tools` has no commits yet — it sits exactly at main, so the latest Gemini Live state is PR #15 (`ae2ddb9` engine + `219e961` order-safety fix). The implementation itself is in good shape: unconstrained ephemeral token mint ([route.ts](app/api/gemini/token/route.ts)), direct v1alpha WebSocket, field-independent `serverContent` handling with the local `state` shadow (the order-safe fix), explicit 24 kHz playback rate, early-audio buffering, and StrictMode-pure `setTurns` updaters. It matches the checked doc precisely (setup shape, `realtimeInput`, transcription fragments, `turnComplete`/`interrupted` semantics).

## Grounding with Google Search: already there ✅

[use-gemini-session.ts:311](lib/realtime/use-gemini-session.ts:311) already sends `tools: [{ googleSearch: {} }]` in the setup message — exactly what the tools doc prescribes, and it's supported on `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`. Search is executed **server-side by Google**, so no client-side response handling is required; it genuinely works today. Two soft gaps:

1. **No prompt guidance.** The OpenAI engine appends `FIRECRAWL_TOOL_GUIDANCE` ("say 'let me look that up', never read URLs aloud") when tools are live; the Gemini personas' prompts never mention that search exists. The model may use it anyway, but narration/quality is untuned.
2. **Search activity is invisible.** During grounded turns, `modelTurn.parts` can carry `executableCode` / `codeExecutionResult` parts (the doc's search examples log these). Your parser only reads `inlineData` and `text`, so those parts are silently skipped — harmless, but the UI has no "searching…" signal the way OpenAI's `mcp_call.started` sets a caption.

## Function calling: absent ❌

There is no function-calling support in the Gemini engine:

- No `functionDeclarations` anywhere — the setup only declares `googleSearch`.
- The `GeminiServerMessage` type ([use-gemini-session.ts:58](lib/realtime/use-gemini-session.ts:58)) has no `toolCall` or `toolCallCancellation` fields, and `handleMessage` has no handler — if the model ever emitted a tool call it would be silently dropped.
- Nothing ever sends `toolResponse.functionResponses`, which the doc says the client **must** do manually (Live API has no automatic tool-response handling).

Constraints from the doc that will shape the implementation:

- **`gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` is synchronous-only.** `NON_BLOCKING` / `scheduling` async function calling is 2.5-only; on your model the agent goes silent until you send the `toolResponse` — so client-side execution needs to be fast, and a spoken "let me check" can only come from prompt guidance before the call.
- **No remote-MCP equivalent.** Unlike OpenAI Realtime (where Firecrawl MCP runs on OpenAI's servers and the client just passes an OAuth token), Gemini Live tool execution is entirely client-side: handle `toolCall.functionCalls`, run the function yourself, reply with `{ toolResponse: { functionResponses: [{ id, name, response }] } }`. A Firecrawl-parity path would mean the browser calling Firecrawl (or an app API route proxying it) from the `toolCall` handler — though note native `googleSearch` already covers the web-lookup use case Firecrawl serves on OpenAI, so function calling here is really for *other* actions.
- **`toolCallCancellation` matters for you specifically** because barge-in is server-VAD driven: if the user interrupts mid-tool-call, the server cancels it and you should drop the pending execution rather than send a stale response.
- Search + functions compose fine: `tools: [{ googleSearch: {} }, { functionDeclarations: [...] }]`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The three engines split tool execution differently: OpenAI runs MCP tools *on its own servers* (client only configures), Gemini runs `googleSearch` server-side but functions *client-side only*, and xAI currently has neither. So "tools" isn't one abstraction across engines — Gemini function calling forces an execution loop into the browser hook itself.
- The unconstrained ephemeral token (no `liveConnectConstraints`) is what makes this all client-configurable — a constrained token would pin the `setup` payload server-side, and adding `functionDeclarations` would then require touching the mint route too.
